subject: Dedicated capacity SKU and eviction/safety-margin for Helix AI (DEAL-9347)
messages:
From: Susan Liu <susan@helix.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helix.ai, Anthony Wu <anthony.wu@helix.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity SKU and eviction policy — Helix AI

Connor / Irene,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We're trying to close sizing for the dedicated capacity line item in our SOW and need one last piece from Redwood: a recommended SKU mix and the eviction/preemption behavior you intend to apply for our reserved pool.

Quick background: our main production workload will be a retrieval-augmented generation service with 1.6k tokens median, 36k tokens worst-case (batching expected). Peak concurrent requests are expected ~60 per minute during business hours (US), and a night batch job will run large-context fine-tuning calls (very expensive).

Questions we need answered before sign-off:
- Which GPU SKU do you recommend as the default for our reserved fleet (H100 / A100 / L4) given the above profile?
- What headroom margin do you provision per instance for model KV/cache and unexpected ME(Memory Expansion) spikes?
- What's your preemption/eviction policy for burst usage — will you evict long-context jobs or drain spot-like instances first?
- Any suggested quantization/partitioning to reduce memory pressure while preserving accuracy?

I've attached our inference profile (helix-inference-profile.csv) and the current SOW draft (SOW_draft_v1.pdf). We'd like to finalize the commitment by EOD Monday to hit our Q4 deployment window.

Appreciate a concise recommendation we can map to the SOW.

— Susan
Susan Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Helix AI
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-08T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity SKU and eviction policy — Helix AI

Internal — forwarding Helix's ask. Key constraints: long-tail 36k tokens; sustained concurrent QPS ~60/min; night batch FT jobs. They want: SKU, headroom margin, eviction behavior, quantization guidance.

My initial read / suggestion to align ops + sales for SOW:
- Default pool: mix H100 + L4. Rationale: H100 for long-context and batch FT (large KV requirements + better FP16 perf), L4 for low-cost stateless real-time traffic. Avoid A100 as primary because it sits between cost/perf and we can't guarantee memory headroom for 36k tails without H100-class memory density.
- Slotting: reserve 35% of reserved capacity as H100 (for worst-case queries and nightly FT), 65% as L4 (for steady-state RAG traffic that can be quantized/streamed).
- Headroom: provision 25% memory headroom for H100 nodes (accounts for KV growth, tokenizer expansions, and safety margin). For L4 nodes, a stricter 40% headroom if used for medium-long contexts — otherwise enforce a context-length cap on L4 routes.
- Eviction/Preemption: soft-evict policy: graceful drain on L4 instances hitting 85% memory; immediate preempt for background FT batch tasks during business hours (migrate to H100 or scheduled window). In practice: allow burst to use dedicated H100 fallback (can be auto-route) but cap L4-sourced long-context queries.
- Quantization: enable int8 quant for L4 workloads and mixed-int8 for certain decoder layers on H100. Offer a model-variant path: fp16 H100 variant + int8 L4 variant with auto-fallback.

Action items for ops: Irene / Priyom — confirm feasibility and operational runbooks (eviction signals, autoscale threshold, migration path for FT batches). Kimberly — I'll need a short blurb on cost delta and SOW wording for the 35/65 split (so sales can map to line items and commit rounding).

I'll prepare a short note back to Susan summarizing once we lock the ops bits.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com <irene_chooi@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-08T18:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity SKU and eviction policy — Helix AI

Connor — good summary. Ops notes and constraints:

- H100 ops: H100 is the safe default for the 36k token tail and nightly FT. We need to reserve NVLink-enabled H100 variants (80GB) to avoid cross-node KV spillage for large contexts. If they insist on cheaper H100 alternatives (lower mem), we'll have to shard KV aggressively which adds latency and complexity.
- L4 ops: excellent cost/throughput for token-scaling, but 40GB L4 limits on KV; enforce a strict 16k token request cap on any L4 route. Implement token-aware routing in the gateway: requests with expected long context go to H100.
- Headroom & soft-evict: 25% on H100 is reasonable. For L4 set soft-evict at 75% (not 85%) because these GPUs have less margin before OOM and we want earlier routing to H100. Soft-evict means: return 429 + Retry-After for stateless calls, and for multi-step jobs attempt transparent reroute to H100.
- Background FT: tag those jobs and schedule into a reserved H100 window overnight. If customer wants them in-business-hours, we need explicit permission to preempt L4 real-time capacity or add burst H100.
- Observability: include token-level tail metrics in the SOW — 95/99/99.9 percentiles for context length + per-route eviction counts (this supports quality escalation).

Priyom: can you confirm the autoscale thresholds (CPU/GPU memory margin signals) and whether we can implement token-aware routing by next week? If yes, we'll finalize the SOW language.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal, Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-09T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SKU and eviction policy — Helix AI

Susan / Anthony — quick confirmation from our side after ops review:

1) Recommended SKU mix (SOW-ready):
   - Reserved pool: 35% H100 80GB (NVLink-enabled) + 65% L4 40GB.
   - H100 will be the official long-context & batch FT pool; L4 will serve low-latency RAG requests with int8 quantization.

2) Headroom & limits:
   - H100 memory headroom: 25% reserved for KV/cache growth.
   - L4 memory headroom: 40% if used for anything >16k tokens; otherwise enforce 16k cap.

3) Eviction / preemption behavior (SOW wording):
   - Soft-evict on L4 at 75% memory pressure: requests that cannot be served will receive a 429 + Retry-After; token-aware routing will transparently route eligible requests to H100 where possible.
   - Background FT jobs will be scheduled into reserved H100 windows overnight. If Helix requests daytime FT, we will either (a) deploy temporary H100 burst nodes (additional cost), or (b) preempt L4 real-time capacity with prior approval.

4) Quantization and model variants:
   - We will provide an int8-quantized L4 variant and an fp16 H100 variant; automatic fallback to H100 if L4 quantized variant violates latency/quality SLOs.

Attachments: capacity-plan-helm-20261009.xlsx (capacity numbers & pricing), SOW_draft_v1.pdf (updated with SKU language).

Next steps: Anthony/procurement — please confirm acceptance of the 35/65 SKU split and the soft-evict SOW language by EOD Monday so we can finalize the invoice and schedule capacity.

Thanks,
— Connor
